clue.text: Borderland music

definitions.meaning: a ... is a frontier district, as in the Welsh ...
a ... is a piece of music for ... to

explanation.definitionFit: A frontier territory is a march, and so is a stirring military tune in strict time.

clue.text: Wiltshireman qualified for Apollo trip

definitions.meaning: The nickname for natives of Wiltshire, from smugglers who claimed to be raking the moon's reflection out of a pond
someone ready to rake over the lunar surface, as on an Apollo moon mission

explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Wiltshire are nicknamed after the legend of yokels raking a pond for the moon, and a lunar explorer would rake the moon.

clue.text: Horses that did so got Bill into debt

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Betting on horses landed someone's account in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is a link word; 'Horses that did so' defines a verb of running in competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses that ran against each other in a contest competed at speed, as on a racecourse.

clue.text: Is not barefooted in the family pew

definitions.meaning: split as ..., wears something on the feet
kneeling cushions found in church pews

explanation.definitionFit: Wearing footwear means one has socks on, and church kneelers are found in pews.

clue.text: Wartime cover for the Lorelei ?

parts.note: the Lorelei is a siren of the Rhine, so her cover would be a siren's outfit; also the one-piece garment pulled on during air raids

explanation.surface: A question about what a Rhine siren wore in the war.
explanation.walkthrough: A siren suit was the zip-up one-piece pulled on over nightclothes when the air-raid siren sounded in the Second World War; the Lorelei is the siren of German legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-piece wartime boiler suit was named after the air-raid warning, and the Lorelei is a legendary siren.

clue.text: Opening for money to make machinery work

definitions.text: Opening for money to make machinery work

parts.words: Opening for money to make machinery work
parts.note: the narrow aperture in a coin-operated machine

explanation.surface: Describes the coin aperture on a vending machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated machine has a narrow aperture into which money is put to start it.

clue.text: Limited balance — credit anyhow

parts.note: the balance is the rest, what remains

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the letters of credit are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bank account with only a small balance and credit handed out carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' is not a bank balance but what remains; 'anyhow', meaning in a careless way, is the anagram signal on the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept within bounds or confined is limited.

clue.text: Latest is we're comfortably housed

indicators.note: housed tells us one piece is lodged inside another

parts.note: comfortably housed suggests snug in a nest
we are, with 're as a link

explanation.surface: The latest news is that we are living comfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comfortably housed' leads to a snug nest, and 'housed' lodges the pronoun inside it; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent thing is the most novel, the most modern.

clue.text: Starry-eyed little honey lover

parts.note: a small bear, fond of honey, made of stars, the northern constellation

explanation.surface: Describes a dreamy young sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'honey lover' looks like a sweetheart; it is a bear, and the starry little bear is the constellation the Little Bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bears are famous for loving honey, and the Little Bear is a northern constellation of stars.

clue.text: River to suit one man in a boat

annotationWithheld.why: River to suit one man in a boat (5): TWEED is a river and a suit cloth, but no reading found for 'one man in a boat'; a search of the exact clue gave nothing
annotationWithheld.clue: River to suit one man in a boat

clue.text: "How all do inform against me ' (Hamlet)

parts.words: How all do inform against me
parts.note: the missing word of Hamlet's soliloquy line, the plural noun meaning events or chances

explanation.surface: A gapped line from Hamlet's soliloquy in Act 4.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is Hamlet's 'How all occasions do inform against me', and the dash marks the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap in Shakespeare's line is filled by a plural noun meaning happenings or opportunities.

clue.text: Was with Lawrence initially in the desert

parts.note: taken as written
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials T and E

explanation.surface: Someone was out in the desert alongside Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' here means Lawrence's own initials, T.E., not the first letter of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is a barren tract of land, a wilderness or wasteland.

clue.text: Pompeii's last news of Vesuvius ?

parts.note: the freshest news is said to be glowing hot, and the last thing Pompeii got from the volcano was literally glowing lava

explanation.surface: What the doomed town last heard from the volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot news is the very latest; the final news Pompeii had of Vesuvius in AD 79 was glowing lava.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking news is called hot, and molten lava from an erupting volcano glows at searing heat.

clue.text: Taken for granted by Lake Tanganyika in 1871

definitions.meaning: at Ujiji on the lake in 1871 Stanley greeted the explorer with 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?'

explanation.walkthrough: Henry Morton Stanley found David Livingstone at Ujiji, on Lake Tanganyika, in 1871 and is famously reported as saying 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?'
explanation.definitionFit: To assume something is to take it for granted, and Stanley's famous greeting used that very verb.

clue.text: So a secret stays that way

definitions.text: So a secret stays that way

parts.words: So a secret stays that way
parts.note: a secret remains a secret only while nobody lets it out

explanation.surface: A remark about how confidences are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence remains one only while untold, not revealed to anyone.

clue.text: Trifle with criminal dexterity, say

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: to nick is to steal, and a knack is a skill, so a thief's skill is a nick knack

explanation.surface: Someone toys with a thief's sleight of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; the thief's 'nick' plus 'knack' sounds exactly like the word for an ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket or ornament of little value is a trifle.

clue.text: Power of a wire-puller

parts.note: a wire-puller works behind the scenes, pulling strings like a puppeteer, and wields sway

explanation.surface: Describes the hold of a backstage schemer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire-puller pulls strings behind the scenes, and that kind of sway over others is called clout.

clue.text: Cut-price bargain ?

definitions.meaning: a small cut made with scissors
in British slang a ... is something cheap, a real bargain

explanation.definitionFit: A scissor stroke is a snip, and in British slang so is a bargain at a low price.

clue.text: Was this pigeon taken for a ride ?

definitions.text: Was this pigeon taken for a ride ?

parts.words: Was this pigeon taken for a ride
parts.note: a pigeon that rides along carried by someone else, also the extinct North American species

explanation.surface: Asks whether a gullible pigeon was swindled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken for a ride' looks like being swindled; read literally it is being carried along, and the passenger pigeon was a real North American bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone carried in a vehicle is a rider, and the passenger pigeon was a North American species.

clue.text: Accommodation in the news

definitions.meaning: the letters N, E, W and S stand for the four compass points

explanation.definitionFit: Lodgings are called quarters, and the four compass points that spell news are the cardinal points or quarters.

clue.text: Swarming to put the fire out

indicators.note: with 'put the fire out' the fire is put out of shape, so its letters are rearranged; that 'the fire' also holds the answer backwards is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Someone is told to extinguish a blaze while it is teeming with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FIRE into the answer; 'to put the' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming or abundant, as a place infested with pests is said to be rife with them.

clue.text: Home protection for the Military Command ?

definitions.text: Home protection for the Military Command ?

parts.words: Home protection for the Military Command
parts.note: domestic screens set before a hearth, read as an order '...!' given to soldiers

explanation.surface: A question about how the army protects its homes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as screens before a hearth, this is home protection; split as 'Fire, guards!' it is an order to troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Screens placed in front of an open hearth protect a home, and the same words make an order to shoot.

clue.text: Promise to end up on the shelf

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word up

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A promise to finish one's days unmarried, left on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts P above LEDGE; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn undertaking or vow is a pledge.

clue.text: Run to share accommodation

definitions.meaning: to double is to run, as soldiers move 'at the double'
to bunk with someone else in one room

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who double are running; people who pair off in one room to save space are also said to do this.

clue.text: "Now -s the milk-white peacock like a ghost" (Tennyson)

definitions.text: "Now -s the milk-white peacock like a ghost" (Tennyson)

parts.words: Now -s the milk-white peacock like a ghost
parts.note: the missing verb in Tennyson's lyric Now Sleeps the Crimson Petal, meaning sags or hangs down

explanation.surface: A gapped line from Tennyson's poem in The Princess.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's line is 'Now droops the milk-white peacock like a ghost'; the dash with -s takes the bare verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb meaning sags or hangs limply fills the gap in Tennyson's line.

clue.text: Paddy's tongue worn out

definitions.meaning: Paddy is a nickname for an Irishman, and his tongue is his accent
a stout shoe, worn out of doors

explanation.definitionFit: An Irish accent is called a brogue, and so is a sturdy outdoor shoe.

clue.text: Dirt in the stern quarter

parts.note: stern means grim
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Muck found in the back part of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern quarter' suggests the back of a ship; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrained filth or soot is grime.

clue.text: Try to wake a Dutch village up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: dorp is the Dutch and Afrikaans word for a village

explanation.surface: Attempting to rouse a sleepy village in Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DORP.
explanation.definitionFit: Poking someone to rouse them is a nudge or jab.

clue.text: Had an entry in the town edition

indicators.note: the answer has entered the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Someone got a mention in the local paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'town edition'.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have it, so possessed in the past tense.

clue.text: It has you on your knees half the time, said Kipling

definitions.text: It has you on your knees half the time, said Kipling

parts.words: It has you on your knees half the time, said Kipling
parts.note: Kipling's poem The Glory of the Garden says half a proper gardener's work is done upon his knees

explanation.surface: A Kipling remark about an activity that keeps one kneeling.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Glory of the Garden Rudyard Kipling wrote that 'half a proper gardener's work is done upon his knees'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending flowerbeds means weeding and planting on your knees, as Kipling observed of the gardener's lot.

clue.text: Masqueraded as the Young Chevalier ?

definitions.meaning: Charles Edward Stuart, the Young Chevalier, was called the Young Pretender, so he acted as a pretender to the throne

explanation.walkthrough: Bonnie Prince Charlie, claimant to the British throne in 1745, was known as both the Young Chevalier and the Young Pretender.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning is masquerading, and claiming a throne made Charles Stuart a pretender.

clue.text: Wherewith Achilles could kill or cure

definitions.text: Wherewith Achilles could kill or cure

parts.words: Wherewith Achilles could kill or cure
parts.note: in Greek legend the wound made by Achilles' weapon on Telephus could be healed only by rust from that same weapon

explanation.surface: A riddle about the Greek hero's double-edged weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Telephus, wounded by Achilles, was told only the wounder could heal him, and rust scraped from Achilles' weapon cured him.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles' weapon, a long shafted lance, wounded Telephus and then healed him in the myth.
